yesterday.note: LIVE read, date range Yesterday (Sep 9, 2026). THE SEP 8 EFFICIENCY GAIN FULLY REVERSED AND THEN SOME -- THIS IS THE WORST DAY ON RECORD FOR THIS ACCOUNT. Spend $60.83 (UP $28.04, +86%) bought only 682 impressions (DOWN 835, -55%) and 20 clicks (down 8, -29%), at a $3.04 average CPC -- up from $1.17 on Sep 8, a 160% increase in cost per click in a single day. Put plainly: yesterday cost nearly twice as much and delivered less than half the reach. CTR did rise to 2.93% from 1.85%, but that is the arithmetic of a collapsing impression base, not improving quality. SPEND BREACHED THE ACCOUNT BUDGET. The account daily budget is $40.00 and Sep 9 spent $60.83 -- 52% over. Brewhouse Dinner alone spent $30.00 against a $15.00/day budget, exactly 2x, on just 105 impressions and 8 clicks at a $3.75 CPC. Brewhouse Lunch spent $30.83 against $25.00/day for 577 impressions and 12 clicks. Google permits daily overdelivery against a monthly cap, so this is not an error, but two campaigns overspending simultaneously on falling volume is the pattern that empties a monthly budget early. CONVERSIONS READ 0.00 and remain flagged pending; an in-product banner still credits Brewhouse Dinner with 1 conversion 'this week, an increase from 0 last week'. Conversion counts stay unreliable at this reporting lag. STRUCTURAL FLAG UNCHANGED AND NOW THE LIKELY CAUSE, NOT BACKGROUND NOISE: both live Search campaigns still read 'All ads limited by policy, Limited by search volume'. An impression base that halves while CPC triples is what a tightening policy limitation looks like. This has persisted across many runs. The policy manager pass is no longer a nice-to-have. Account budget $40.00/day; 2 live campaigns, 4 paused, 2 drafts in progress.
